title: Codeforces Topic-wise Practice Sheet
subtitle: Rating 1100–1800 · Contests 2022–2026
summary: 272 problems across 22 topics, ordered as a roadmap. Within each topic, problems go easy → hard.
howTo: Go topic by topic in Step order. Inside a topic, problems are sorted easy → hard (1100 → 1800).
Mark each problem as you go (To do, Attempted, Solved, Revisit). Problems Codeforces accepts, or that pass all their samples here, are marked solved for you.
Give each problem 30–45 min honestly. If stuck, read the editorial, mark it Revisit, and re-solve it a week later without help.
Once you have been through every topic, switch to All problems and practise by rating (e.g. all 1400s).
about: All problems come from the official Codeforces API (problemset.problems + contest.list), pulled 1 Nov 2026.
Filters: rating 1100–1800, contest held 1 Jan 2022 or later. Kotlin Heroes and April Fools rounds excluded.
Each problem appears once, under its most specific topic. Within a topic, picks favour problems many people solved (well-tested, good editorials), spread across ratings.
'Solved By' is the Codeforces solve count at pull time.

Segment Tree / Fenwick / Sparse Table and Binary Trie topics are hand-picked: Codeforces has no tag for them, and at ≤1800 they're often one valid approach among several. The 'Key Technique' column says which one to practise.
Linked lists aren't a Codeforces topic (they're an interview/LeetCode staple). The 'Stacks, Queues, Sets & Maps' section covers the pointer and simulation practice instead.
